question.prompt: Let \(P\) be a cubic polynomial with \(P(0) = k,\) \(P(1) = 2k,\) and \(P(-1) = 3k.\) What is \(P(2) + P(-2)?\)

solutions.explanation:
The requested sum uses opposite inputs. Adding such evaluations cancels the odd powers, so we only need the quadratic and constant coefficients. Write
\[
P(x)=Ax^3+Bx^2+Cx+D,
\]
where \(A\ne0\) because \(P\) is cubic. From \(P(0)=k\), we have \(D=k\). Therefore
\[
P(x)+P(-x)=2Bx^2+2k.
\]
At \(x=1\), the given values yield
\[
2B+2k=P(1)+P(-1)=2k+3k=5k,
\]
so \(2B=3k\). At \(x=2\), it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(2)+P(-2)
&=8B+2k\\
&=4(2B)+2k\\
&=12k+2k=\boxed{14k}.
\end{aligned}
\]
No division by \(k\) is needed, so this also holds when \(k=0\). The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Add values at opposite inputs
